'''Alex Scott''' (born 1967) is a British mathematician, currently Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Oxford]] and Fellow and Dominic Welsh Tutor in Mathematics at [[Merton College, Oxford]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Alexander Scott|publisher=[[Oxford University]]|access-date = 17 August 2025|url=https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/scott/}}</ref>

==Early life==
As a sixteen year old schoolboy, Scott wrote the [[role-playing game]] [[Maelstrom (role-playing game)|Maelstrom]] for [[Puffin Books]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Holter |first=Matthijs |date=1 April 2004 |title=Frem fra glemselen |url=https://www.scribd.com/document/52400766/Imagonem-31-web |trans-title=From Oblivion |magazine=Imagonem |language=Swedish |location= |publisher= |access-date=}}</ref>
He took his first degree at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], gaining [[British undergraduate degree classification#First-class honours|first class honours]].

==Career==
From 1993 to 1997, Scott was a Junior Research Fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, where he graduated [[Doctor of philosophy|PhD]] in 1995.<ref name=CV/> His dissertation, titled "Unavoidable Induced Subgraphs", was 
supervised by [[Béla Bollobás]].<ref>[https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=79346 "Alexander David Scott"], mathgenealogy.org, accessed 28 October 2025</ref> From 1996 to 2001 he was lecturer in mathematics at [[University College, London]], then Reader there from 2001 to 2005. In 1997 he was a [[Visiting Professor]] at the [[University of Memphis]]. In 2005 he was elected as a fellow and appointed as Dominic Welsh Tutor in Mathematics at [[Merton College, Oxford]], then in 2006 became Professor of Mathematics in the [[University of Oxford]].
<ref name=CV>[https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/scott/Pages/cv.pdf "Alexander David Scott, Professor of Mathematics"], University of Oxford, accessed 28 October 2025</ref><ref name=":0"/>
